RagShortTexts: The standing military of Thervingians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Thervingians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Thervingians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Horns sound the advance, and the spearmen step forward with shields locked edge to edge. Mounted attackers crash against the front rank while the men behind thrust through the gaps. A soldier who turns his back is cut down by his own file, since retreat without an order means death for the one who runs.

Officers at the rear of the Thervingian host plot the flanks on a cloth map weighted with stones. Victory depends on provisions reaching the wings on time and on keeping every unit in a straight line. Once the center holds, the cavalry can encircle the enemy and seal the trap, and the men who funded the campaign will divide the spoils by rank.
